text:
Verified directly from the three `configure()` blocks — that's the only place auth is applied. Global prefix is `/api` (`src/main.ts:8`).

## Public endpoints (no token required)

| Endpoint | Source | Intended? |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api` | `src/app.controller.ts:5` | yes — hello-world root |
| `POST /api/users` (register) | `src/user/user.controller.ts:32` | yes |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `src/user/user.controller.ts:43` | yes |
| **`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** | `src/user/user.controller.ts:37` | **no — see below** |
| `GET /api/articles` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:24` | yes |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:38` | yes |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:43` | yes |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `src/profile/profile.controller.ts:18` | yes |
| `GET /api/tags` | `src/tag/tag.controller.ts:17` | yes — `TagModule.configure()` is an empty body (`src/tag/tag.module.ts:17-18`) |

Everything else is guarded: `GET|PUT /user` (`src/user/user.module.ts:20`), the eight article routes in `src/article/article.module.ts:24-31`, and `profiles/:username/follow` for all methods (`src/profile/profile.module.ts:22`).

## The one that matters

`DELETE /api/users/:slug` is unauthenticated and deletes by **email**:

```ts
// user.controller.ts:37-40
@Delete('users/:slug')
async delete(@Param() params) { return await this.userService.delete(params.slug); }

// user.service.ts:83-85
async delete(email: string): Promise<DeleteResult> {
  return await this.userRepository.delete({ email: email });
}
```

No token, no ownership check — anyone who knows a user's email address can delete that account. It's absent from `UserModule`'s `forRoutes` list, which only covers `GET /user` and `PUT /user`.

## Two things that look like protection but aren't

- **`@ApiBearerAuth()`** sits on all four controllers (e.g. `user.controller.ts:14`, `tag.controller.ts:10`). It's a Swagger annotation only — it documents a lock icon, it enforces nothing. Same for the `@ApiResponse({status: 403})` lines on the article controller; nothing in the codebase returns 403.
- **`@User('id')` on a public route** (`profile.controller.ts:19`) decodes the token itself when middleware didn't run (`user.decorator.ts:13-17`). That's optional identity, not a guard — it returns `undefined` with no token. It also means `GET /profiles/:username` with a *malformed* token throws out of `jwt.verify` uncaught → 500 rather than 401, the same bug `LESSONS.md:29-36` records for the middleware.

Want me to draft a fix for `DELETE /users/:slug` — add it to `UserModule`'s `forRoutes` and switch it to delete the caller (`@User('id')`) instead of an arbitrary email?
